## What it is

A repository template with no product code and no workspace: the agent setup Figentra Flow renders
(`.agents/`, `.claude/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`), the GitHub setup (code owners, the ruleset, issue
and pull request forms, the Quality Gate), the pinned toolchain (`mise.toml`), git hooks
(`lefthook.yml`), formatting, spelling, secret scanning, Renovate and the security policy.

Infrastructure, the testbed, Flow and brand start from it. A Stackra product starts from
[figentra/stackra-template](https://github.com/figentra/stackra-template) instead, which is this
layout plus a Stackra workspace (Stackra ADR 0528).

## Status

**In progress**: the first layout, from the repo standards of 2026-11-06.

The states: **Live** (in use), **In progress** (being built), **Planned** (no build yet).

## Quick start

```bash
gh repo create figentra/<name> --template figentra/neutral-template --private
mise install
fflow sync
```

Then add what the repository needs (a workspace, members, `tools/`) and declare any extra root entry
in package.json `stackra.layout.allow`, with the reason (Stackra ADR 0526).

## Architecture at a glance

| Path                         | What it holds                                                        |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `docs/`                      | the repository's own docs (Stackra ADR 0526 decision 2)               |
| `flow.config.json`, `.flow/` | Figentra Flow's preset and README data; `fflow sync` renders the rest |
| `.github/`                   | code owners, the ruleset, forms and the Quality Gate                  |
| `mise.toml`, `lefthook.yml`  | the pinned tools and the git hooks                                    |

## Development

Install the dependencies with the repository's package manager, then run the same checks CI runs before you open a
pull request.

Changes go through `fflow`, a spec-first workflow.

| Step                          | Command                                        |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Spec the change               | `/flow-specify`, `/flow-clarify`, `/flow-plan` |
| Start a worktree for an issue | `fflow start <key>`                            |
| Run the gate on the branch    | `fflow gate run`                               |
| Land the pull request         | `fflow land`                                   |
| See specs, worktrees and PRs  | `fflow status`                                 |
| Re-render this README         | `fflow readme`                                 |

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. Open an issue before a large change, so the approach is agreed before the work
starts.

Each branch and pull request names its issue's key, each commit is a Conventional Commit, and a pull request lands
once its checks pass and its review is approved.
